newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - April 1.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Prime Minister John Howard last night met China's Premier Li Peng in an attempt to embark on an historic reshaping of relations between the two countries. Howard offered China a newly independent and practical relationship based on economic interests. Te attempt to reconcile the two countries is one of the Howard Government's most important foreign policy developments so far. Page 1.

Federal Transport Minister John Sharp has revealed he is considering proposals for a system of fines for airlines operating late flights. The scheme would be similar to those operating at many large airports in Europe and the United States and would be used in a bid to reduce costly delays at Sydney Airport. Page 1.

According to the superannuation industry, the Senate impasse over the superannuation surcharge legislation may delay the collection of the first A$500 million in revenue from the scheme. The Labor Party, with the support of the Democrats and Greens, has put forward amendments aimed at safeguarding low-income earners from the legislation, but until the legislation is in its final form, superannuation trustees are unwilling to implement systems to collect members' tax file numbers and recover the surcharges Page 3.

The US has issued a strong warning to Federal Industry and Science Minister John Moore, saying it will not tolerate the use of industry assistance schemes that breach international trade rules. The meeting held between Moore and U.S. Trade Representative Carlene Barshefsky focused on fresh U.S. concerns over the A$5 million compensation package given to Howe Leather by the Federal Government. Page 3.
THE AUSTRALIAN

During a 90-minute meeting between Prime Minister John Howard and Chinese Premier Li Peng at the Great Hall of the People yesterday, Howard proposed a series of economic and human rights initiatives, including a "dialogue on human rights" and the securing of a deal which will see China send a feasibility team to Australia to assess a process for streamlining steelmaking. Page 1.
Violence to go in X-rated clean-up

Federal Cabinet is today expected to endorse a plan for the Australian Capital Territory to co-operate with the States and the X-rated video industry to remove excessive violence and the depiction of under-age sex from videos. However, the plan does not iclude any moves to shut Canberra down as the soft-porn capital of Australia. Page 1.

Texas-based Australian golfer Steve Elkington shot a three-under-par 69 to win the A$801,629 Players Championship in Florida yesterday - golf's most important event outside the four majors - by a record margin. The win places the 34-year-old at the top of the US tour money list with A$984,400 in just four events this year. Page 1.

Twenty one-year-old Daniel Millard followed a strong family tradition yesterday when he pipped favourite Evan King by one tenth of a second in a dramatic finish to the A$30,000 Stawell Gift foot race - his grandfather William won the first Gift in 1878 afer training for six weeks. Page 1.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Before holding talks with senior Chinese officials, including President Jiang Zemin and Premier Lo Peng, Prime Minister John Howard told a group of Beijing businessmen China and Australia could forge a relationship of great mutual benefit built on the strngths of the past. Page 1.

A crowded public gallery in the Bangkok Central Criminal Court was shocked yesterday as Lyle Patrick Doniger, Jane Dawson and Deborah Letitia Spinner - three Sydney drug addicts - were each sentenced to 50 years' jail for trafficking heroin. The three were accused of trying to carry 115 grams of heroin onto a flight from Bangkok to Sydney in March last year. Page 1.

The Palliative Care Association of New South Wales estimates that 20,000 patients in the State miss out on palliative care each year and some experts say many terminally ill patients are forced to consider euthanasia because they do not have access to such care. The PCA says another 200 practitioners, including 50 medical specialists are needed. Page 1.

A group of six children, led by a 16-year-old boy, walked about 60 kilometres through bush in Western Australia then guided searchers to seven other children, including a seven-month-old baby, and 27-year-old Wanda Schultz who were stranded for two days ater their car broke down. Page 1.
THE AGE

Despite an unexpectedly tough stance on human rights by Prime Minister John Howard during formal meetings with Chinese Premier Li Peng, yesterday's meeting between the two leaders held a positive tone. Howard outlined a closer economic and political partnership between the two countries which he said would take both partners into a new era. Page 1.

Three former Australian drug addicts have been found guilty of trafficking heroin in a Bangkok court, and sentenced to 50 years' jail. Lyle Patrick Doniger, Jane Dawson McKenzie and Deborah Letitia Spinner were initially sentenced to life imprisonment for attempting to export the heroin, but the four judges hearing the case reduced the sentence to 50 years after the three confessed to carrying the drugs, but denied they were involved in a conspiracy to export. Page 1.

Victorian Parliamentary Secretary for Planning and Local Government Bruce Atkinson has told The Age there was no conflict of interest involved with his working as a consultant for councillors in the Western Australian town of Kalgoorlie, saying he had contiuned his consultancy work to interstate and New Zealand since his appointment to the Victorian Government last year. Page 1.

A 16-year-old boy led six children through 60 kilometres of heavy scrub to safety, and guided searchers back to seven young children and one woman, after the group was stranded in the Western Australian goldfields for two days when their car tyre went fla. A wide search by 70 people and three aircraft failed to find the bush tucker gatherers. Page 1.
